In Trancoso, it is easy to split the day between the beach and Quadrado. This green square, surrounded by low, colorful houses, has become the most recognizable place in this settlement on the Bahia coast. At its far end stands a white church, with an ocean view beyond it. Trancoso is part of the municipality of Porto Seguro and combines seaside relaxation with walks through the historic village.

Quadrado rewards a closer look: the colors of its walls, wooden doors and handmade goods in small shops. By day, the square is bright and spacious; in the evening, restaurants and lights draw people back. It is a lovely place to linger over a meal and sample Bahian cuisine. Fish or seafood moqueca and acarajé introduce local flavors through distinctive dishes.

Near the village are Coqueiros and Nativos beaches. They offer a taste of Trancoso's coastline, where sand, palms and ocean fill the day. For longer excursions, consider Rio da Barra and Taípe. It is best to choose a beach and plan the route around the weather, tides and how long you want to spend there.

Trancoso suits travelers who want to alternate beach time with evening strolls and good food. After the sightseeing portion of a trip, it is a welcome pause by the sea: walk along the sand, return to Quadrado's colorful houses and watch evening fall near the white church.

## A road through the wetlands

Beyond Poconé begins the Transpantaneira, the road travelers follow into the Northern Pantanal. Its unpaved stretches and bridges cross wetland landscapes, so wildlife watching starts during the drive itself.

On the Araras Ecolodge itinerary, there are stops along the road for photographs and observing birds and other animals. The route to the lodge follows roughly the first 32 kilometers of the Transpantaneira.

It is worth looking not only straight ahead, but also toward the water, trees and open areas on either side of the road. Each stop depends on what nature is doing at that moment.

Trenque Lauquen is in western Buenos Aires Province. On a journey through Argentina's interior, it offers a chance to trade the pace of long drives for an evening in town and a glimpse of local life.

For an agricultural delegation, the town serves as a base before visits to farms. It is a practical place to combine overnight accommodation and meals before continuing south through the province. We arrange the itinerary so that professional visits alternate with relaxation after time on the road. Trenque Lauquen is a good choice for travelers who want to see Argentina's farming heartland through working farms and small towns.

Tres Arroyos connects town life with rural surroundings and the Atlantic coast of the municipality of the same name. Beyond town lie small settlements and agricultural landscapes, and the route can continue on to the sea.

In our agricultural program, we use Tres Arroyos as a stop between field visits, meetings at educational institutions and the drive to Necochea. It is a good place to spend the night after a full technical day. When planning a business trip, we arrange the visits so participants have time to discuss the technologies they have seen and exchange impressions.
